brief:
The S&P 500 rose 0.47% as traders watched a bond sell-off, while the Nasdaq gained 0.53% on a tech rally, amid concerns about a potential rate hike by the Federal Reserve.

S&P 500 (+0.47% to 7740.62): Market Rallies on Bond Sell-Off. Traders are watching the easing of a bond sell-off, which is supporting the market's rise. The S&P 500's gain is attributed to the decrease in bond yields, which is seen as a positive sign for the market. [3]
Nasdaq (+0.53% to 27081.55): Nasdaq Rises on Tech Rally. The Nasdaq rose 0.53% to 27081.55 as hedge funds increased their bets on tech stocks, driven by the AI rally, [5]. This move suggests traders are optimistic about the sector's performance, [1]. However, the rally was partially offset by a decline in Nvidia, a key tech stock, [6].
10-Year Yield (+0.46% to 5.19): Treasury Yields Surge Amid Rate Hike Fears. Traders are watching the Federal Reserve's signals on rate hikes, which has led to a surge in Treasury yields. The 10-year yield rose 0.46% to 5.19, its highest level since 2007, as investors bet on future interest rate increases. [7] [9] [10]
USD/JPY (-0.66% to 157.22): USD/JPY Sell-Off. The USD/JPY pair fell 0.66% to 157.22, driven by a brief dollar sell-off after Japan's financial chief discussed financial ties with the US. [11] Traders are watching Japan's stance on trade and financial cooperation, which may impact the dollar's value. [11] [14]
Crude Oil (-3.21% to 91.57): Oil Prices Plummet Amid Iran Tensions. Crude oil prices fell 3.21% to 91.57 as markets awaited news on the Iran truce, but traders remained cautious about potential attacks on oil facilities. The decline in oil prices was also linked to a weaker US dollar, which made crude oil more expensive for importers. The uncertainty surrounding the Iran situation kept traders on edge, leading to a sharp sell-off in oil prices.
Gold (+0.69% to 4327.6): Gold Rises on Rate Hike Bets. Gold rose 0.69% to 4327.6 as traders shifted their focus from inflation concerns to the likelihood of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve, which could boost the dollar and reduce gold's appeal. [19] Reuters reported that mounting rate hike bets kept weekly losses in sight for gold, while [20] Yahoo Finance noted that gold prices fell as inflation concerns steadily mount. [21] Kitco stated that gold prices will hit $4,900/oz in 2026 on strong sovereign demand, but this forecast was not directly related to the current price move. [22] USA Today reported a 2.37% fall in gold prices on the same day, but this was not the same as the 0.69% gain seen in the current price. No clear catalyst appeared in the news to explain the current price move.

- The Dow edged higher at open, with bond selloff abating as oil price slips, as traders await the Federal Reserve's signals on rate hikes.
- The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq rebounded as oil prices eased and Treasury yields pulled back, driven by a brief dollar sell-off after Japan's financial chief discussed financial ties with the US.
